zh.title: 漢莎航空削減兩條美國航線空中巴士A380航班轉載亞洲
zh.summary: 漢莎航空縮減兩條美國航線之空中巴士A380航班；運能將轉派至兩條亞洲航線。
body: 根據航空媒體 Simple Flying 報導，德國漢莎航空（Lufthansa）已決定削減兩條主要美國航線上的空中巴士A380（Airbus A380）巨無霸客機航班。這項營運調整代表該航空公司針對跨大西洋市場之長程客運運力進行階段性排程優化。
漢莎航空規劃將這些調整所釋出的空中巴士A380機隊運能，暫時轉移部署至一對亞洲航線上，以平衡不同區域市場的客運需求。這項區域間的運能重劃屬於暫時性措施，反映出航空公司彈性調配旗艦寬體客機機隊的營運策略。

en.title: Lufthansa Reduces Airbus A380 Flights on Two US Routes to Redeploy Capacity to Asia
en.summary: Lufthansa is cutting Airbus A380 flights on two US routes to temporarily redeploy capacity to Asian routes.
body: German flag carrier Lufthansa has decided to cut its Airbus A380 flight capacity across two major routes serving the United States, according to reporting by aviation news outlet Simple Flying on August 18, 2026. The flight reductions mark a temporary adjustment in the airline's long-haul passenger service allocation across its transatlantic network.

In place of the reduced transatlantic services, Lufthansa will temporarily redeploy the freed Airbus A380 capacity onto a pair of routes in Asia. The airline is shifting its superjumbo aircraft to better balance passenger demand across different geographical markets, representing a temporary realignment of its widebody fleet deployment.

zh.title: 退役QantasLink Fokker F100飛抵Shellharbour機場將成為航空博物館展品
zh.summary: 退役QantasLink Fokker F100已降落Shellharbour機場(WOL)，將由Historical Aircraft Restoration Society(HARS)作為公眾展示；該機註冊VH-NPU、名稱Meekatharra，為QantasLink第二架捐贈予HARS的F100。
body: 退役QantasLink Fokker F100已降落Shellharbour機場，將成為Historical Aircraft Restoration Society(HARS)的公眾展示。
該機註冊VH-NPU、名稱為Meekatharra，由QantasLink捐贈，為該航空公司第二架交予HARS的Fokker F100，之前一架於2026年2月捐贈予HARS的帕克斯博物館。
Meekatharra於2016年12月加入QantasLink機隊，在此之前曾為美國航空和奧地利航空服役，累計飛行超過11,250小時、約九百萬公里、共7,543班次，載運約一百萬名乘客，主要服務西澳洲地區資源產業。
QantasLink目前西澳洲網路每週運航超過600班次，目的地包括25個區域機場以及達爾文、紐卡素、霍巴特、聖誕島和科科斯(基靈)群島，機隊包含40架Fokker 100、空中巴士A319和A320。
QantasLink正逐步淘汰Fokker F100機隊，改為引進巴西航空工業E190以提升可靠性、燃油效率和乘客舒適度，首架E190預計下月抵達珀斯機場(PER)。
QantasLink董事總經理Mark Dal Pra表示，Meekatharra在連接西澳洲地區社區方面發揮了近十年的重要作用，並感謝HARS志工將繼續傳承該機的故事。
HARS總裁暨首席飛行員Bob De La Hunty指出，該機將與Qantas首架波音747-400(VH-OJA)和一架前Qantas波音707-138一同展出，有助於說明連接西澳洲社區與支撐產業的航空歷史。

en.title: Retired QantasLink Fokker F100 Lands at Shellharbour Airport for Museum Display
en.summary: A retired QantasLink Fokker F100 has landed at Shellharbour Airport (WOL)       and will become a public exhibit with the Historical Aircraft Restoration Society (HARS); the aircraft, registered VH-NPU and named Meekatharra, is the second F100 donated by QantasLink to HARS.
body: A retired QantasLink Fokker F100 has landed at Shellharbour Airport , where it will begin a new life as a public exhibit with the Historical Aircraft Restoration Society (HARS).

The aircraft, registered VH-NPU and named “Meekatharra,” was donated by QantasLink and became the second F100 the airline has given to HARS, after another was donated to the organization’s Parkes Museum in February 2026.

Meekatharra began flying for QantasLink in December 2016, having previously served with American Airlines and Austrian Airlines. Over its time with QantasLink it logged more than 11,250 flight hours and roughly nine million kilometers across 7,543 flights, carrying an estimated one million passengers throughout regional Western Australia while supporting the region’s resource industry.

QantasLink’s broader Western Australian network currently operates more than 600 flights per week to over 25 regional destinations, along with routes to Darwin, Newcastle, Hobart, Christmas Island, and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands. Its current Western Australian fleet includes 40 aircraft across the Fokker 100, Airbus A319, and Airbus A320 types.

QantasLink is gradually retiring its F100 fleet in favor of Embraer E190 aircraft, aimed at improving reliability, fuel efficiency, and passenger comfort. The airline’s first E190 is expected to arrive at Perth Airport (PER)       next month.

Mark Dal Pra, Managing Director of QantasLink, said Meekatharra played an important role connecting regional communities across Western Australia for close to a decade. He added that HARS has become a natural home for some of the airline’s retired aircraft, helping preserve important parts of Australian aviation history, and thanked the volunteers who will help ensure the aircraft’s story continues to be told.

Bob De La Hunty, President and Chief Pilot of HARS, said the organization was honored that QantasLink entrusted it with another significant piece of Australian aviation history. He noted that Meekatharra will join Qantas’ first Boeing 747-400 and a former Qantas Boeing 707-138 in helping tell the story of the aircraft that connected regional communities and supported industry across Western Australia, adding that HARS volunteers remain passionate about keeping those stories alive for visitors.

zh.title: 阿斯塔納航空延長暫停杜拜航班至2026年9月30日
zh.summary: 阿斯塔納航空延長暫停哈薩克至杜拜航班至2026年9月30日；10月復飛後將減班
body: 阿斯塔納航空（Air Astana）延長暫停其哈薩克與杜拜之間的航班至2026年9月30日，理由為海灣地區持續不穩定。
該中亞航空公司表示，已同時調整2026年10月阿拉木圖—杜拜及阿斯塔納—杜拜航線的班表，在服務恢復後將降低航班頻率。
受影響旅客可獲免費改訂同一訂位艙等的機票，旅行日期至2026年11月20日。旅客亦可於原購票點申請全額退款，或免費改訂至阿斯塔納航空其他國際目的地，惟須支付適用的票價差額。
此次延長是該航線在2026年屢遭中斷的最新一章。阿斯塔納航空先前曾因空域限制暫停阿聯酋航班，其後於2026年7月4日恢復阿斯塔納—杜拜直飛服務，並於8月初擴大至每日航班。
然而恢復營運不久後即告中止。2026年7月12日，阿斯塔納航空因區域軍事緊張局勢升高引發新的安全疑慮，再次暫停該航線，其中KC205航班自阿斯塔納飛往杜拜途中被迫折返，另一架自阿拉木圖出發的KC897航班在起飛前取消。
其後暫停多次延長，先延至2026年7月21日，再延至2026年8月31日，航空公司當時援引荷莫茲海峽及更廣泛海灣地區局勢進一步惡化。阿斯塔納航空並非唯一調整海灣營運的業者；加拿大航空、法國航空、荷蘭皇家航空及新加坡航空等其他國際航空公司近月也延長或維持暫停飛往杜拜及其他中東目的地的航班。

en.title: Air Astana extends suspension of Dubai (DXB) flights through September 30, 2026
en.summary: Air Astana extends Kazakhstan-Dubai flight suspension to September 30, 2026; October schedule to reduce frequency upon resumption
body: Air Astana is extending the suspension of its flights between Kazakhstan and Dubai until September 30, 2026, citing continued instability in the Gulf region.
The Central Asian carrier said it has also adjusted its October 2026 schedule for the Almaty (ALA)-Dubai and Astana-Dubai routes, reducing flight frequency once service does resume.

Affected passengers are being offered free rebooking within the same booking class for travel through November 20, 2026. Travelers may also request a full refund at their original point of purchase, or rebook onto other Air Astana international destinations without penalty, subject to any applicable fare difference.

The latest extension is the newest chapter in a route that has faced recurring disruption throughout 2026 as tensions in the Middle East have escalated. Air Astana had suspended UAE flights earlier in the year due to airspace restrictions, before resuming nonstop Astana-Dubai service on July 4, 2026 and expanding to daily flights by early August.

That resumption proved short-lived. On July 12, 2026, Air Astana suspended the route again after rising military tensions in the region created fresh safety concerns, with one flight, KC205 from Astana to Dubai, forced to turn back mid-journey and another, KC897 from Almaty, cancelled before departure.

The suspension was subsequently extended multiple times, first to July 21, 2026 then through August 31, 2026, as the airline cited what it described as further deterioration of the situation in the Strait of Hormuz and the wider Gulf region. Air Astana is not alone in adjusting its Gulf operations; other international carriers, including Air Canada, Air France, KLM, and Singapore Airlines, have similarly extended or maintained suspensions to Dubai and other Middle Eastern destinations in recent months.
